vision.oneLine: How the C&AG and chartered accountants audit public sector undertakings, from compliance to performance, propriety and comprehensive audit.
vision.why:
This chapter is short but keyword-driven. The exam gives a short fact pattern and asks "which type of audit is this?" or "which step of planning?". Once you can sort cues into financial, compliance, performance, propriety and comprehensive audit, most marks follow.

Performance audit alone accounts for about 16 ICAI questions in the five-year sweep.

items: Whom the C&AG audits; Audit Boards
Four parts: review, appraisals, resume, results

sixty: PSU forms: Departmental, Company, Corporation. A government company has not less than 51% Government shareholding.
C&AG: Article 148 appoints, 149 powers, 150 form of accounts, 151 reports laid. Term 6 years or age 65.
For a government company the C&AG appoints, directs, comments, and may order supplementary and test audit.
PAC checks legal, authorised, re-appropriated. COPU does the same for PSUs. Estimates Committee suggests economies.
Financial audit is attestation. Performance and compliance are generally direct reporting.
Performance audit: economy, efficiency, effectiveness. Planning has nine steps A to I; the ADM has five columns.
Propriety audit uses Kohler's tests and can criticise spending that follows the rules.
Comprehensive audit combines financial, compliance and performance audit.
The C&AG's PSU report has four parts: review, appraisals, resume, results.

askedAs.how: A short fact pattern; name the type of audit and justify it.
Which of steps A to I is the team at? (RTP Nov 2026 Q18).
Audit Boards, COPU, 3 Es, propriety audit, comprehensive audit.
Section numbers, committees, number of steps or columns.
A line such as "casual vacancy 30 days" becomes a full timeline case.

pitfalls: Calling a propriety audit a performance audit (SM TYK 7).
Forgetting that listing does not end government company status at 51%.
Mixing up the C&AG's sections: 143(5) direct, 143(6)(a) supplementary, 143(6)(b) comment, 143(7) test.
Saying financial audit is direct reporting.

levels.title: What a public sector undertaking is
levels.hook: Three forms, and the 51% line that decides which audit rules apply.

teach.html: A PSU is owned or controlled by the Central Government, any State Government(s), or partly by the Centre and one or more States. Three forms: (1) departmentally managed undertakings (Indian Railways, Postal Services); (2) government companies and deemed government companies under the Companies Act, 2013; (3) corporations set up under specific Acts (LIC, UTI). Memory: D-C-C: Departmental, Company, Corporation.
Under s.2(45) of the Companies Act, 2013: not less than 51% of paid-up share capital held by the Central Government, State Government(s) or partly both; includes a subsidiary of such a company.
PSUs supply basic inputs (coal, oil, steel, cement, fertilisers) and public utilities (railways, telecom, electricity, road transport). That is why audit extends beyond accounts to value for money.

levels.correlate: The 51% test returns in Level 3 (who appoints the auditor) and stays even if the company lists its shares.

recall.q: Minimum Government shareholding to be a government company (%)?
recall.why: Not less than 51% of paid-up share capital (s.2(45)).

recall.q: LIC is an example of…
recall.why: Corporations set up under specific Acts: LIC, UTI.

recall.q: Indian Railways is a government company.
The three forms in the SM order.
A subsidiary of a government company is also a government company.
recall.why: s.2(45) includes a subsidiary of such a company.

twist.q: The Government holds 51% of a company that has now listed its shares. Is it still a government company?
twist.a: Yes. Listing or disinvestment does not change the status while the Government holds at least 51%, so the C&AG's role continues (SM TYK 5).

levels.title: The C&AG: Articles 148 to 151 and reach
levels.hook: Appointed, powers, form of accounts, reports: four Articles, four verbs.

teach.html: Art. 148: appointed by the President; removal only by a special procedure; salary set by Parliament. Art. 149: duties and powers, prescribed by Parliament (the DPC Act, 1971). Art. 150: form of Union and State accounts, prescribed by the President on the C&AG's advice. Art. 151: reports go to the President (Union) or the Governor (State), who lay them before Parliament or the Legislature. Memory: 148 Appoint, 149 Powers, 150 Form, 151 Reports.

DPC Act, 1971: term of 6 years or up to age 65, whichever is earlier; resigns by letter to the President. The C&AG with the Indian Audit and Accounts Department is the Supreme Audit Institution of India.

(1) Union and State departments and offices, including Railways and Posts and Telecommunications; (2) public commercial enterprises (government companies and corporations); (3) non-commercial autonomous bodies owned or controlled by the Union or States; (4) bodies substantially financed from Union or State revenues. The scope and extent of audit is determined by the C&AG himself.

A unique IAAD feature: Audit Boards carry out comprehensive appraisals of PSUs in diverse sectors, associate experts, and discuss findings with management and ministries before finalising. They are not separate legal entities.

levels.correlate: Art. 151 is the destination of every report: Level 9 shows the C&AG's PSU report; Level 4 shows the committees that scrutinise it.

recall.q: Which Article provides that C&AG reports are laid before Parliament via the President?
The C&AG's term is 6 years or up to which age?
recall.why: 6 years or up to age 65, whichever is earlier.

recall.q: The President prescribes the form of accounts on the C&AG's advice (Art. 150).
Audit Boards are separate legal entities.
recall.why: They work under the supervision and control of the C&AG.

recall.q: Order the Articles 148 to 151 by their verbs.

twist.q: A State department's compliance audit report is ready. To whom does the C&AG submit it?
twist.a: To the Governor of the State, who causes it to be laid before the State Legislature (Art. 151). For Union accounts the recipient is the President.

levels.title: Auditing government companies (sections 139, 143)
levels.hook: Five section references, five powers of the C&AG. Often asked with the 60 and 30-day clocks.

teach.h: Powers of the C&AG over a government company
teach.html: While government equity is 51% or more, the C&AG appoints the auditors (CA firms), gives directions on how the audit is conducted, comments on their report, and may order a supplementary audit and a test audit.

s.139(5)/(7): C&AG appoints or re-appoints; remuneration fixed by the company within C&AG guidelines. s.143(5): directions; the auditor's report covers the directions, action taken and impact on accounts. s.143(6)(a): supplementary audit within 60 days of receiving the report. s.143(6)(b): comment on or supplement the report; placed before the AGM. s.143(7): test audit by order.
Filled by the C&AG within 30 days; if not, the Board fills it within the next 30 days.

levels.correlate: Comments from 143(6)(b) feed the C&AG's report on government companies (Level 9).

recall.q: Which section lets the C&AG direct the manner of audit?
Days within which the C&AG may conduct a supplementary audit after receiving the report?
The members appoint the auditor of a government company at the AGM.
Casual vacancy: days for the C&AG, and then days for the Board, are each…
recall.why: 30 days for the C&AG; failing that, 30 days for the Board.

recall.q: The s.143(5) report replaces the auditor's other s.143 reports.

twist.q: Vacancy arises on 1 March (non-leap year). The C&AG does not fill it. What is the last day on which the Board may act?
twist.a: C&AG window: 30 days, to 31 March. Board window: the next 30 days, to 30 April. So the Board can act up to 30 April.

levels.title: Parliamentary financial committees
levels.hook: PAC, Estimates Committee and COPU: one-line cues decide the answer.

teach.html: Scrutiny by the whole Parliament would be impractical, so audit reports and accounts stand referred to specialised committees.

PAC: satisfies itself that money was legally disbursed on the purpose, expenditure was authorised, and re-appropriation followed the rules (PAC = Legal, Authorised, Re-appropriated). It controls government departments. Estimates Committee: examines estimates for economies and administrative reform, suggests alternative policies, checks money is well laid out, and the form of estimates. COPU: the same financial control as the PAC but over public undertakings: reports and accounts, C&AG reports, autonomy and efficiency, sound business principles.
The C&AG is the committees' "friend, philosopher and guide". Committees present reports; Ministries report action taken; committees present Action Taken Reports.

levels.correlate: Cue: a committee examining a PSU's performance and pending action on C&AG findings is COPU (SM TYU 1). Reports reach committees through Art. 151 (Level 2).

recall.q: Which committee exercises over PSUs the control that the PAC exercises over departments?
Which committee suggests economies and alternative policies on the estimates?
The PAC checks that expenditure was authorised.
The Estimates Committee comments on a policy already approved by Parliament.
recall.why: It does not comment on approved policy, though it flags policies that waste.

recall.q: Order the follow-up after a committee report.

twist.q: A committee examines whether a steel PSU is managed on sound business principles and prudent commercial practices. Which?
twist.a: COPU: its function includes examining the autonomy and efficiency of public undertakings and whether they follow sound business principles.

levels.title: Scope, elements and principles of PSU audit
levels.hook: Fiscal vs managerial accountability, three parties, attestation vs direct reporting, 8 principles.

teach.html: PSU audit is not limited to financial and compliance audit: it extends to performance, propriety and comprehensive audit. Two accountabilities: fiscal (provision of funds, sanctions, compliance, propriety) and managerial (efficiency, economy, effectiveness).

Three parties: auditor (SAI India), responsible party, intended users. Subject matter, criteria and subject matter information. Type of engagement: attestation (the responsible party measures the subject matter and the auditor concludes on it) or direct reporting (the auditor measures it). Financial audits are always attestation; performance and compliance audits are generally direct reporting.

General (8): ethics and independence; professional judgement, due care and scepticism; quality control; audit team management and skill; audit risk; materiality; documentation; communication. Process: plan, conduct, report and follow up.

levels.correlate: The attestation/direct split decides how each of Levels 6 to 8 is framed. Fiscal vs managerial accountability separates Level 6 from Level 7.

recall.q: Financial audits are always…
Number of general principles of PSU audit?
In a direct reporting engagement the responsible party measures the subject matter.
recall.why: In direct reporting the auditor measures or evaluates it.

recall.q: Efficiency, economy and effectiveness belong to which accountability?
Order the audit-process principles.
recall.why: Plan, conduct, report and follow up.

twist.q: An audit checks only whether expenses accord with public interest and accepted customs, and the C&AG rejects it as a performance audit. Right?
twist.a: Yes. That is propriety audit, not performance audit; a performance audit examines economy, efficiency and effectiveness (SM TYK 7).

levels.title: Financial and compliance audit
levels.hook: Opinion on statements versus conformity with rules: regularity plus propriety.

teach.html: An opinion on whether the financial statements are prepared, in all material respects, in accordance with the applicable framework; for a fair presentation framework, presented fairly or a true and fair view. Always an attestation engagement.

Whether activities, transactions and information comply in all material respects with the rules governing the entity. It covers regularity (formal criteria from laws, regulations, agreements) and propriety (sound financial management and ethical conduct of officials). Done with the audit of financial statements, separately, or with performance audit. Process: plan, perform and gather evidence, evaluate, report (with entity responses) and follow up.

levels.correlate: Exam cue: records do not match the rule in the law (buildings wrongly classified; water charges under-collected) points to compliance audit.

recall.q: Compliance audit is concerned with…
Compliance audit can be done together with performance audit.
recall.why: Non-compliance may then be a cause, explanation or consequence of the performance.

recall.q: Compliance audits are generally attestation engagements.
An insurance PSU issues policies without the required actuarial valuation. Which audit?
recall.why: Non-compliance with required approvals and rules: compliance audit.

recall.q: Order the compliance audit steps.

twist.q: Water charges are under-collected because the department applied the wrong rate table. Compliance or performance?
twist.a: Compliance audit: the records do not follow the rule in the law or regulations (regularity). It becomes a performance issue only if the question is about economy, efficiency or effectiveness of the programme.

levels.title: Performance audit: 3 Es, planning, criteria and approach
levels.hook: The highest-weight topic (about 16 ICAI questions in 5 years). Learn the nine planning steps.

teach.html: An objective, systematic examination of evidence to assess the performance of an organisation, programme, activity or function. Economy: minimising the cost of resources for the right quantity and quality (cheap inputs). Efficiency: input-output ratio (maximum output for minimum input). Effectiveness: extent to which objectives are achieved (intended against actual impact).

Evaluate the 3 Es of policy, programmes, organisation and management; promote accountability and transparency. Responsibility for measurable objectives and indicators rests with the departments or heads of entities.

(A) Understand the entity; (B) Objectives and scope; (C) Criteria; (D) Approach; (E) Questions; (F) Skills and expertise; (G) Audit Design Matrix; (H) Timetable and resources; (I) Intimate the entity. Understanding the entity uses documents of the entity, legislative documents (PAC/COPU/Estimates reports), policy documents, research, past audits and stakeholder inputs.

Criteria come from: procedure manuals; policies and guidelines; criteria of other entities; expert opinion; scientific knowledge; management literature. Approach methods: analysis of procedures, case studies, existing data, surveys, analysis of results, quantitative analysis. Audit Design Matrix columns: objective, questions, criteria, evidence, data collection and analysis method.

Strategic planning, planning individual audits, implementation (preliminary study, field audit, draft report to the entity), report approval, performance audit report, follow-up and impact assessment.

levels.correlate: RTP Nov 2026 Q18: a team gathering entity records, legislative discussions, committee reports, prior audits, research and stakeholder inputs is at stage (A), understanding the entity.

recall.q: Minimising the cost of resources for the right quantity and quality is…
The input-output ratio is…
How many planning steps (A to I) are suggested?
How many columns does the Audit Design Matrix have?
recall.why: Objective, questions, criteria, evidence, data collection and analysis.

recall.q: Order the first four planning steps.

twist.q: A steel PSU's modernisation was delayed and missed favourable market conditions. Which audit is this, and what would you examine under each of the three Es?
twist.a: Performance audit (SM chapter-opening case). Economy: was the modernisation resourced at the lowest cost for the right quantity and quality, and in due time? Efficiency: output achieved against inputs. Effectiveness: were the modernisation objectives actually achieved?

levels.title: Comprehensive and propriety audit
levels.hook: Two audits examiners ask in the same breath. Learn the Kohler test and the subjectivity problem.

teach.html: An efficiency-cum-performance audit that combines financial, compliance and performance audit for a holistic view: were objectives fulfilled, value for money obtained, targets achieved? Areas include investment decisions, capacity utilisation, production performance, labour productivity, idle capacity, costs and prices, materials management, sales and credit control. Criteria: Bureau of Public Enterprises guidelines, industrial engineering and technical studies, standards of financial propriety.

Verification of transactions on the tests of public interest, commonly accepted customs and standards of conduct (E.L. Kohler). It brings out improper, avoidable or infructuous expenditure even though incurred in conformity with existing rules. Four principles: expenditure not more than the occasion demands (ordinary prudence); no authority sanctions expenditure to its own advantage; funds not used for a particular person or group; no other avenue to indirectly benefit management or others. Examples: a building not used for its purpose is infructuous; a school used five years after completion is avoidable expenditure.

"Propriety" is a moral term, so verifiable propositions are hard to formulate. Judge decisions in the circumstances when taken, not on hindsight. Over-subjective judgment would dampen management initiative.

levels.correlate: Compare with performance audit (Level 7): propriety asks "was it fair and prudent?"; performance asks "were the 3 Es achieved?". The Compare tab drills this.

recall.q: Who stated the tests of public interest, commonly accepted customs and standards of conduct?
Number of principles of financial propriety listed in the SM?
Propriety audit looks only at expenditure that breaches rules.
recall.why: It also looks at expenditure incurred in conformity with rules that is improper, avoidable or infructuous.

recall.q: Comprehensive audit combines financial, compliance and performance audit.
A school building used five years after completion is…
recall.why: Avoidable expenditure; a building never used for its purpose is infructuous.

twist.q: An auditor criticises a manager for taking a flight when a train could have been used. The manager shows the train would not have delivered the same result in time. Fair criticism?
twist.a: No. Judge decisions in the circumstances when they were taken, not on hindsight. Air travel is not wasteful unless rail was feasible with the same result.

levels.title: The C&AG report and the exam round-up
levels.hook: Four parts of the report, then a one-page map of all the audit types.

teach.html: (a) Introduction with a general review of working results of government companies, deemed government companies and corporations; (b) results of comprehensive appraisals by the Audit Board; (c) resume of company auditors' reports under C&AG directions and comments on the accounts; (d) significant results of audit of undertakings not taken up by the Audit Board. Reports go to the President or Governor under Art. 151.

Opinion on statements: financial. Rules and law: compliance. 3 Es: performance. Fairness, public interest, avoidable and infructuous spending: propriety. All together for the whole undertaking: comprehensive.

solves.tip: Count the days left in the month you start, then add whole months. 60 days from 10 January: 21 days to end of January, 28 in February (non-leap), that is 49, so 11 more into March.

hooks.story: Picture one question for each: Financial, "are the numbers true and fair?". Compliance, "did they follow the rules?". Performance, "was it cheap, productive and did it work?". Propriety, "was it fair and prudent?". Comprehensive, "all of the above for the whole undertaking". When a fact pattern appears, ask which question it is really asking.

The PAC inspects whether the money trail is legal. COPU inspects public undertakings like a business consultant. The Estimates Committee is the budget editor: it looks at the numbers before they are spent and suggests economies.
